lecture_title: Sound, Quantum Oscillators, and the Second Law

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: The molecular-speed estimate, pressure derivative, and ideal-gas substitution are simultaneously visible and sufficiently unobstructed.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Compare the speed of sound with the thermal molecular velocity.
assets.caption_hint: molecular and pressure-derivative estimates for the speed of sound

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: The room-air constants and the resulting speed are visible without lecturer obstruction.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The estimate gives roughly five hundred meters per second.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: The spring-mass sketch and kinetic-plus-potential Hamiltonian appear together at the introduction of the oscillator.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Write the oscillator energy in terms of momentum and displacement.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: The partition function is cleanly factorized into momentum and position Gaussian integrals.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The exponential of the sum separates into two Gaussian factors.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: The full board preserves the Gaussian result, logarithm, beta derivative, and final energy in one contextual frame.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Each Gaussian contributes one half of the temperature.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: The discrete oscillator sum and geometric-series identity are centered and readable.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: For the quantum oscillator the state count is a true sum.
assets.caption_hint: quantum partition function as a geometric series

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: The thermal mean-energy expression is complete and directly precedes the temperature limits.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Differentiate the logarithm of the quantum partition function.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_09.png
assets.rationale: The low-temperature exponential suppression is visible beside the exact mean-energy formula.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: At low temperature the excitation energy is exponentially small.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_10.png
assets.rationale: Several string normal modes are clearly superposed, matching the argument about infinitely many oscillator frequencies.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: A continuous string is an infinite collection of normal modes.
assets.caption_hint: normal modes of a vibrating string

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_11.png
assets.rationale: The compact initial phase-space patch and coordinate axes are visible before deformation begins.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Begin with a compact probability patch in phase space.
assets.caption_hint: initial probability patch in phase space

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_12.png
assets.rationale: The fine black filament and red finite-resolution cells are both visible at the point where coarse-graining is introduced.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The exact snake keeps its area while finite-resolution cells cover more.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_13.png
assets.rationale: The bounded accessible region appears beside the filament and coarse cells, directly supporting the finite-volume argument.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Positions and momenta remain within a finite accessible region.

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_14.png
assets.rationale: The evolved filament fills the bounded region while the earlier coarse-grained construction remains visible for comparison.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Chaotic stretching carries a special patch through the accessible region.
assets.caption_hint: chaotic filamentation through accessible phase space

assets.name: lecture_07_figure_15.png
assets.rationale: The complete double-pendulum sketch is visible and directly anchors the final discussion of deterministic chaos.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The double pendulum is chaotic even without friction.
assets.caption_hint: double pendulum as a deterministic chaotic system
